description: Scenario: async task holding the auth_failure_tracker std::sync::Mutex panics (e.g. due to an unexpected None unwrap in record_failure). std::sync::Mutex becomes poisoned; all subsequent .lock() calls return Err and are silently ignored via .unwrap_or(false) in lifecycle.rs. After a single task panic, auth failure tracking stops entirely — the lockout mechanism is silently disabled for all future sessions. Use tokio::sync::Mutex to eliminate poison semantics in async code, or convert the tracked-set eviction to not require a guard across an await point.
title: std::sync::Mutex used for auth_failure_tracker in async context — poison risk
